verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — Hormuz Drone Strike Reverses Oil Bear Thesis; KOSPI Circuit Breaker; Russell Recon Close Creates Whipsaw
verdict.rationale_short: Three compounding overnight developments push the morning framework from HOLD to STEP ASIDE. First, an Iranian drone struck a cargo vessel in the Strait of Hormuz Thursday evening, pausing the UN ship evacuation and driving Brent crude from $72.50 (June 25 close) to $74.43 premarket — directly reversing the 'Hormuz normalization' disinflation narrative that anchored the prior three briefings. Second, Asian markets accelerated their selloff: KOSPI fell 5.81% to 8,411 (intraday -8%, triggering a 20-minute circuit breaker), Nikkei 225 fell 4.40% to 69,185. Third, MU slipped ~4% premarket after Morningstar warned AI memory revenue could peak in 2028 then halve by 2029-2030 due to supply glut — the first institutional bear case against the blowout MU earnings. Separately, NYT reported OpenAI may delay its IPO to 2027, sending SoftBank (largest OpenAI backer) -13% in Tokyo. ES futures -0.5% imply SPX open ~7,322 (138 pts below 7,460 regime floor); NQ futures -1.2%. All four primary regime gates remain breached for the third consecutive session. NVDA provides the session's lone counter-signal: opened at $202.17 (up from $193.53 June 25 close) as Growth ETFs position ahead of the Russell Reconstitution effective at today's 4 PM close, where NVDA now holds the #1 slot in the Russell 3000. Verdict: STEP ASIDE — do not chase the morning trend in either direction; let Russell reconstitution noise clear before re-evaluating Monday. UMich Consumer Sentiment final release (10 AM ET; preliminary 48.9) is today's only macro catalyst before the close.

bear_case: Counter-argument: The Hormuz drone strike represents a direct breach of the Iran-US normalization framework, and if Iran extends 'transit fee' enforcement beyond a single incident — which the UN evacuation pause suggests is possible — Brent toward $80-85 by July Fourth reintroduces the CPI upside risk the market believed was resolved by the Iranian shipping deal. A $10/bbl sustained rise in Brent adds approximately 0.3-0.5 pp to headline CPI within 45 days, enough to shift BofA's September hike from 'possible' to 'certain.' OpenAI delaying its IPO to 2027 removes a primary catalyst for AI multiple expansion: if OpenAI cannot IPO, what does that signal for the monetization timeline of NVDA's Vera Rubin, CRWV's $99B backlog, and MU's $50B Q4 guidance? KOSPI triggering a circuit breaker for the second time in four sessions — after a +5.42% 'recovery' on June 25 — suggests the June 23 MSCI-driven decline was not the low. If SPX closes below 7,300 today, three straight failed recoveries above 7,460 convert the floor to resistance and the STEP ASIDE framework escalates to BEARISH for the week of June 30. Invalidation: Iran publicly retracts 'transit fee' demands AND Brent falls back below $72 within 48 hours — then thesis reverts to HOLD.
